recognize_zh: 周邊血液可見三顆芽細胞，其中兩顆併排、核形不規則或有凹陷、染色質細緻、細胞質少而淡藍無顆粒，背景血小板稀少並有淚滴狀紅血球；6 歲女童貧血、血小板低加上此型態，須懷疑急性淋巴母細胞白血病。
features: Three circulating blasts, small to medium in size (about 1.5–2 times a red cell)
High N:C ratio with irregular, focally indented nuclear contours
Scant pale blue agranular cytoplasm without Auer rods
Background mild anisopoikilocytosis with occasional teardrop cells; platelets reduced
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows mild anisopoikilocytosis with occasional teardrop cells and decreased platelets. Three blasts are present in this field; they are small to medium-sized with a high N:C ratio, irregular to indented nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and scant agranular pale blue cytoplasm. No Auer rods or granules are seen. In a 6-year-old with anemia and thrombocytopenia, findings are suggestive of acute lymphoblastic leukemia, confirmed as T-lineage by flow cytometry.

ddx.vs: Morphologically identical and more common in children; flow cytometry (CD19 vs cytoplasmic CD3) is required.
Reactive lymphocytes have abundant cytoplasm that hugs adjacent red cells and more condensed chromatin, without anemia and thrombocytopenia of marrow failure.
Myeloblasts often show granules or Auer rods and more cytoplasm; MPO and myeloid antigens separate them.
